subject: alchemistWorkbench
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: alchemist's workbench with potions, books, scales and herbs.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a Genshin-style wooden workbench scene with potions, books, scales, and herbs—static, no joints, built using part/lathe/extrude/sweep primitives with SVG textures, aiming for a substantial but manageable file.

I'm working out dimensions for the bench and its components: top slab, legs, lower shelf, and a back rack of shelves, then helper functions for boxes with cel-painted wood grain, gold trim, and an alchemical emblem decal on the front apron.

Now I'm designing potions as lathe-shaped flasks with glowing liquid, cork tops, and gold bands in a few varieties, plus a stack of covered books with cream pages and gold spines, an open book on a lectern with rune-covered pages, and an alchemical scale with a post, beam, chained pans, and a gold pivot.

I'm adding herb bundles hanging from a rack with leaf-textured cards, a potted plant, and a mortar and pestle, along with a glowing candle, a cyan crystal reminiscent of an Anemo element sitting on a small base, a back shelf with gabled gold ornamentation holding bottles, and a small cauldron with glowing green liquid. Now I'm writing the lathe geometry code for these shapes.

Still writing geometry code...

Writing potion generator function...

I'll give the whole bottle a single glow colour at strength 0.7 plus gold collar and cork, skipping a separate glass shell for simplicity. For the rack, I'm placing uprights at x=±0.85 reaching from floor to y=1.8, positioned behind the bench at z=-0.42, with shelves at y=1.15 and 1.45 sized 1.7 wide by 0.2 deep.

Adding a gold-trimmed cornice up top with a hanging rail at y=1.75 for herb bundles, plus shelves stocked with potions and books, and a dark back panel. I'm adjusting the upright positions to ±0.88 and z=-0.45 to avoid overlapping the bench top, checking the depth math so the rack sits cleanly behind without clipping.

Now laying out bench-top items: scales near center, mortar and open book slightly forward, a cauldron to the right, and a front row of potions and candles arranged across the remaining space.

Working out the scales piece specifically: a lathed base disk, a post, a beam with hanging pans attached via chain rods, with weights on one side and herbs on the other to balance it. Defining color constants...

Now I'm designing a front apron emblem combining a hexagram alchemy symbol with a vision-style circle and star, placing it as a glowing gold-line plane over the wood apron panel, possibly repeated across the front.

For the open book, I'm building a lectern with two tilted cover boxes and page planes forming a V shape, with the outer edges rising from a low central spine to suggest an open book sitting at an angle.

Setting up the up-vector so the page faces backward correctly, then placing a box for the lectern base at the book's position. Now sketching the cauldron as a lathe shape, working out the profile points for the outer belly curve and rim before closing the loop back to the axis.

Adding the liquid surface as a glowing green disc, simple cone feet, a gold torus rim and handle arc, and a few glowing bubble spheres above the cauldron. Moving on to the mortar, starting its stone lathe profile with the base and rim curve points.

Now sketching the pestle as a tilted rod, then a scaled octahedron crystal with cyan glow sitting on a small gold lathe base, and a cream candle with an orange glowing flame cone on a dish. For the hanging herbs, I'm placing bundle cards along the rail with alternating lavender and green leafy textures, tied with small cylinder bands and string rods.

Next I'm building a terracotta lathe plant pot with ringed leaf cards, then a bookRow function generating boxes of varied size and flat color palettes with thin gold spine bands facing forward, including one leaning book. Finally setting up the floor legs as square posts positioned at the four corners under the top slab.

Now I'm adding a lower shelf plank with stretchers, populating it with jars, a sack, bottles, and a stack of books, plus gold corner caps and trim boards on the bench top. I'm also planning the texture set (emblem, page, herbs, label, leaf) and considering a glowing rune circle or sign plaque on the back panel.

Writing SVG code...

Now I'm planning the card rendering system - a part() helper for geometry and glow effects, a box rotation helper using degree inputs, and a potion definition map before writing the potion() function itself.

Building out the potion() function: generating a lathed bottle shape with cork, gold collar ring, and a label plane positioned using stored radius and height offsets per potion kind.

Now I'm working out shelf and rack positioning: potion bottles sitting on shelf surfaces at specific heights, with two shelves and a top cornice, plus figuring out where to hang herbs from a rail so they don't overlap the upper shelf's items.

Better idea: hang herbs from side arms extending out from the uprights at the outer edges, keeping them clear of the shelf contents. I'm checking clearances for a front cornice rail with hanging bundles against the shelf2 items' depth to confirm there's no overlap in the z-axis.

Now I'm placing six bundles across the x-axis under the cornice, verifying their vertical extent against the shelf2 items' heights to avoid collisions, then positioning a plaque sign centered on the cornice front and checking it doesn't clash with the bundles since they sit at a lower y and different z depth.

Adding gold finials atop the uprights and setting overall proportions, then moving into the actual code build: setting up the RNG seeding helper, flame glow geometry, and scale pan weights.
